leaks_found: A1, narrow, not a data leak: the protocol's own entry can be replaced by a regular file (a copy or a hard link of another file) between the path rule and the read. The look is then accepted on that file's text, because the identity check compares the open file with the protocol path as it is after the swap. Making the same replacement before the run (no race) gives the same result, so it is an edit of the protocol's file and needs write access to lab/. The judged text's sha256 is recorded in the meta and the marker, so a swap-and-restore would show up as a sha256 that matches no version of the protocol. No data is read.

Guard coverage, not on the look's code path: tarfile.open in the 5 stream modes ('r|*', 'r|', 'r|gz', 'r|bz2', 'r|xz') opens the file with os.open (tarfile._LowLevelFile), so the guard never sees it, although the docstring says tarfile is covered in every mode. pyarrow.orc readers also bypass the guard and are not named. Shown on absent paths only; nothing was read.
No leak found that lets the look read data at or after 2026-01-01, a holdout path, or (through a link race) a file other than the one at the protocol's path.
fixes_needed: Small, vhi_guard.py only; the spec sha256 does not change; re-run proofs.py afterwards. Pin the protocol's identity when the path rule runs, so that a rename or replace of the protocol's entry between the path rule and the read is refused, as check (a) requires. In resolve_cut_declared, right after declared_path_check, take os.stat and os.lstat of DECLARED_PATH. Pass (st_dev, st_ino) to declaration_check, and accept the descriptor only if it matches that pinned identity as well as the current one. Add 2 proof-i rows (entry replaced by a copy, and by a hard link). This does not stop a replacement made before the run, which is an edit of the protocol. Optional, medium: also require the judged text's sha256 to equal the committed PROTOCOL_V3.md at HEAD, so that a temporary swap cannot carry the look.

Tiny (docstring) or small (wrap), vhi_guard.py: tarfile's stream modes 'r|...' open with os.open and are not refused. Either correct the docstring ('every mode except the stream modes r|..., which open with os.open: not covered') and list them under NOT COVERED with pyarrow.orc, or wrap tarfile._LowLevelFile.__init__ with the open() check in reading mode and add the 5 modes to the fix 4 probes.

Not a harness fix, the lead's step before the look: the declaration text in PROTOCOL_V3.md is still absent (0 'autopsy_HI_look', 0 spec sha256). It must quote autopsy_HI_look and b71f69d59999bdb97442bf0a1beff9a8512b883396886323426e69e55e277960, plus item 5 of the previous recheck. That is: the single access line replaces the per-read logging; synthesis A's five run through the payoff lens's variants.py; the check first gates synthesis A's five only (confirmed: K1-K3 are still judged when it fails).

Optional, tiny: let proofs.py take an output folder (for example an environment variable for OUT and the proof j/k rehearsal paths), so an independent reviewer can re-run it without touching lab/. The A3 CSV probes still need a path under lab/.
